title: dsh-task-profile-v1
description: Epic P4-02's generic compiled TaskProfile: the reference back to the user goal every inference traces to (must[1]), hard and soft constraints each carrying their own source and confidence (must[1], acceptance[1]), a side-effect classification in P2-04's vocabulary (acceptance[2]), and the questions an ambiguous or high-risk missing field produced instead of a guess (must[2]). Mirrors packages/run/task-profile/src/types.ts's TaskProfile field-for-field for readers outside TypeScript; the two semantic rules a shape cannot carry -- an unknown-default side effect reporting a confidence other than 0, and a question about a field the profile also decides -- are enforced by that package's validateTaskProfile and are deliberately absent here. additionalProperties is false throughout: must[0] restricts the profile to generic fields, and an unrecognised key is where a vertical one would arrive.

goalRef.description: must[1]'s reference to the originating user/message session event. A reference, never a copy of the goal text: the session log owns that fact.

provenance.description: must[1]'s source and confidence for one inferred field. confidence is a closed [0, 1] real; a user-stated origin is not automatically 1, since a user can state something ambiguously.

constraint.description: One constraint the profile carries. provenance is required on soft constraints as well as hard ones: acceptance[1] names hard constraints, but a soft constraint with no source would be a preference this system invented.

sideEffect.description: acceptance[2]'s side-effect classification. riskClass and ground are P2-04's own vocabulary (@deepseek-ai/dsh-risk-taxonomy), reproduced here rather than re-invented; there is no 'none' member for an unknown effect to be marked with, and 'unknown-default' distinguishes a class nothing decided from one a rule did.

question.description: must[2]'s question: data the profile carries, not a prompt the compiler delivers. The compile step is deterministic (acceptance[0]) and so cannot await a human; asking is left to a consumer that may wait.
